key_insight: PECA reduced mean response length by 72.8% while increasing multiple-choice diagnostic accuracy from 40.8% to 44.0% in a 1.7-billion-parameter model.
clinical_relevance: Shorter outputs could make clinical AI responses easier to review under time pressure, but clinical utility and safety remain unestablished.
method: Adds a differentiable conciseness term to QLoRA supervised fine-tuning.
Encourages end-of-sequence prediction once responses exceed a token budget.
Requires no preference data or auxiliary model and trains on a single commodity GPU.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports fine-tuning on medical-o1-reasoning-SFT and multiple-choice diagnostic evaluation, with a conciseness-strength sweep mapping the accuracy–length trade-off.
watch_item: Multiple-choice accuracy does not establish whether shorter responses preserve safety-critical detail in real clinical workflows.
paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation: Differentiable Length Control for Concise Clinical Reasoning in Smaller Language Models
